Lisa —

Appreciate the quick read. Attached is a first draft that ties three MAP checkpoints to pricing/commit changes (see Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx). High level:

- Checkpoint 1 (POC complete, week 2): Pilot credit + 30% ramp discount for first 30 days.
- Checkpoint 2 (Integration + reliability validation, week 6): Commit tier 1 eligible; 5% ongoing discount on base price if committed throughput >= 50k tokens/day.
- Checkpoint 3 (Production ramp, week 12): Full commit kicks in; additional volume discounts up to 12% depending on committed QPS.

I also included an early-ramp protection clause that limits overage exposure for the first 30 days after production go-live. Attached term-sheet summarizes commit thresholds and sample invoice math (redwood-pricing-term-sheet-v2.pdf).

Would love your feedback on the ramp timing and the discount bands — I can tighten numbers after internal approvals.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- Offer an incentive rebate equal to 5% of month-one invoices if Acme signs a 12-month commit at or above the tier-1 threshold within 30 days of Checkpoint 2. This is additive to the ongoing discount bands.
- For early-ramp protection, prefer a hard cap of $12,500 for month-one overages. Keeps our exposure bounded and looks clean to procurement.
- Confirm discount application applies to entire committed base once threshold is met (rolling 30-day).

Neha — any legal/finance flags on the rebate language or the $12.5k cap? Also copying Jonas for exception approval — this is slightly more aggressive than standard playbook but reasonable for strategic proof-of-concept accounts.
